text:
Sam: Heads-up — saw a tenant surge in prod that exposed a weird interaction between early-ack, kv-cache evictions, and the continuous batcher. sketching a short playbook idea, want quick feedback.
Maya: ugh. timeline?
Sam: happened ~10:08 UTC, sudden spike from a single tenant doing ~3k rps for ~45s. Batcher started coalescing, early-ack path kicked in, but a bunch of requests hit stale kv cache and warmed the model repeatedly.
Devon: so wasted tokens + hotspots on kvcache misses?
Sam: exactly. cost spike + tail latency for other tenants. Nothing crashed but SLOs nudged. infra-bot posted GPU queue pressure alerts.
infra-bot: GPU pool high_utilization=92% queue_length=18 drops=0
Maya: rough. high-level playbook idea?
Sam: propose 3 layering steps: 1) admission-level tenant-surge detection, 2) soft-degradation policies (non-blocking), 3) fallback routing to cheaper model variants or delayed-ack. also clearer signals to kv-cache eviction to avoid churn.
Ricardo: can you unpack "soft-degradation"? sounds like A/B fallback but live.
Sam: short: don't hard-preempt. instead: a) mark tenant as "surge" and apply token-budget backoff (reduce batch size/priority), b) route new requests to a lower-capacity fastpath with stricter length limits, c) enable prefix-caching for recent tokens for that tenant to avoid kv warmups.
Devon: prefix-caching per-tenant sounds heavy. memory blowup concern.
Sam: agreed. think smaller LRU for surge tenants only, TTL 30s, cap by bytes. eviction hint: don't evict global hot keys when a surge tenant is warming cache.
Maya: steps 1 & 2 are doable in admission. step 3 touches kv-cache internals and runtime — needs careful ops flags.
Alexa: can we detect surge purely at edge? e.g., rate delta over window + queued tokens metric
Sam: yes, detection is: if tenant_rps_window_5s > baseline * 20 AND queued_tokens_in_30s > X then mark. baseline is EWMA per-tenant.
Ricardo: and what about early-ack? we rely on it for low latency. We saw early-ack causing duplicate work when fallback retried.
Sam: proposal: tighten early-ack invariant: only early-ack when (a) request matched cache hit hint OR (b) admission token budget is stable. Otherwise hold ack until we know route.
Devon: that means holding ack more often — can harm tail latency for normal requests.
Maya: maybe make it per-tenant adaptive: hold ack only for surge-marked tenants.
Sam: yes that's the plan. minimal impact for normal tenants.
Alexa: ops: what observability do we need? CSR -> make playbook actionable.
Sam: add three dashboards: surge-detection timeline, per-tenant kv-miss-rate, early-ack-hold-rate. and alerts for sustained surge > 2min.
Ricardo: rollout strategy?
Sam: phased: dev canary in staging with synthetic tenant surge, then a small % of canary hosts in prod with feature flag, then ramp.
Devon: any quick config snippet we can use for the feature flag? so SEs can test.
Sam: yep, draft config below:

```
{ "surge_detection": { "multiplier": 20, "window_s": 5, "queued_tokens_threshold": 10000 },
  "soft_degrade": { "kv_ttl_s": 30, "kv_bytes_cap": 10_000_000, "early_ack_policy": "hold_for_surge" }
}
```

Maya: nice. think we also need a rollback trigger: e.g., if global latency > SLO + 10% after rollout, flip off.
Sam: agreed. add automated flip if cluster_p95_latency increases > 15% for 3 consecutive mins.
Alexa: docs + runbook needed for on-call: how to identify false positives and how to force-flag a tenant.
Sam: will draft runbook: steps to inspect dashboards, temporarily disable feature flag, and manual eviction of per-tenant cache entries.
Ricardo: queueing tradeoff note: if we deprioritize surge tenant, their requests queue longer — risk of timeouts from client side. need client-facing guidance (429 vs 202 early-ack decisions).
Maya: prefer 429 when rate-limit enforced, 202 when queued but accepted for processing. clients need to know.
Sam: final open questions: 1) exact kv_cache size cap? (ops input) 2) admission signal thresholds (tune via canary) 3) telemetry labels to add (tenant_surge=true)
Devon: for kv cap I'd start conservative: 10MB per surge tenant as in config, revisit after canary.
Ricardo: I can own canary validation and metric gating.
Maya: I'll take docs + runbook.
Sam: I'll PR the runtime flags and add the dashboards. tagging followups: @Ricardo @Maya @Devon for ownership. thanks.
Alexa: :thumbsup:
